content.text: One POST in Postman, then Data/<resource>.json opened to show the new record, including a field the client couldn't set.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Server-side field generation** is classic API design: the client sends only what it knows (`Name`, `CourseCode`, `Instructor`, `Credits`, `CurrentGrade`), but the server stamps `Id`, `GradePoints` (calculated from grade), and `CreatedAt`. The DTOs enforce this: `CourseRequestDto` has no Id/CreatedAt/GradePoints fields.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Postman setup for the demo:**

```
POST http://localhost:5000/api/courses
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <your-jwt-token>

{
  "name": "Data Structures",
  "courseCode": "CS-301",
  "instructor": "Dr. Smith",
  "credits": 4,
  "currentGrade": "B+"
}
```

**What you'll see in `Data/courses.json` after the POST:**

```json
{
  "Id": 3,              // ← server assigned (next available)
  "Name": "Data Structures",
  "CourseCode": "CS-301",
  "Instructor": "Dr. Smith",
  "Credits": 4,
  "CurrentGrade": "B+",
  "GradePoints": 3.3,   // ← server calculated from B+
  "CreatedAt": "2026-11-19T..."  // ← server timestamp
}
```

The three fields the client couldn't set:
1. **Id** - auto-incremented by `JsonCourseRepository`
2. **GradePoints** - `GradeConverter.ToGradePoints("B+")` → 3.3
3. **CreatedAt** - `DateTime.UtcNow` at creation time

To test: start the API (`dotnet run`), grab a token from `POST /api/auth/login`, hit the POST, then open [Data/courses.json](GritTrack.Api/Data/courses.json).
One validation failure, with the error body on screen, and one 409 from your business rule.

**1. Validation failure (400)** - omit required `name`:

```
POST http://localhost:5000/api/courses
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "courseCode": "CS-301",
  "credits": 4,
  "currentGrade": "A"
}
```

Response body:
```json
{
  "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc9110#section-15.5.1",
  "title": "One or more validation errors occurred.",
  "status": 400,
  "errors": {
    "Name": ["Course name is required."]
  }
}
```

---

**2. Business rule 409** - duplicate `courseCode` (IT-1234 already exists):

```
POST http://localhost:5000/api/courses
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "name": "Another Web Course",
  "courseCode": "IT-1234",
  "credits": 3,
  "currentGrade": "B"
}
```

Response body:
```json
{
  "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc9110#section-15.5.10",
  "title": "Course code already exists",
  "status": 409,
  "detail": "A course with code 'IT-1234' already exists."
}
```

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Two different error tiers**: 400 is automatic from ASP.NET model binding (the `[Required]` attribute on the DTO), while 409 is your explicit business logic in `CourseService.CreateCourseAsync` returning `SaveCourseOutcome.DuplicateCourseCode`. The controller's `DuplicateCourseCodeProblem()` formats the RFC 9110 problem details.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
